semantic_correction.stem: A caregiver says a client taking oral TEMODAR (temozolomide) has difficulty swallowing the capsules and asks whether a capsule can be opened and mixed with food at home. Which response is correct?

options.A: Do not open, chew, or dissolve the capsule; contact the healthcare team because any required opening must be done by a trained hazardous-drug professional.
options.B: Open the capsule and mix the powder with soft food if the caregiver wears ordinary examination gloves.
options.C: Crush the capsule contents into a fine powder and mix them with liquid so the entire dose is easier to swallow.
options.D: Open the capsule at home if direct skin contact is avoided because inhalation and mucous-membrane exposure are not important.

semantic_correction.rationale: Current FDA-approved TEMODAR labeling instructs patients not to open, chew, or dissolve the capsule contents and to swallow the capsules whole with water. If a capsule is damaged, contact with the powder should be avoided because exposure can occur through skin or mucous membranes; affected areas should be washed with water immediately. The label further states that if TEMODAR capsules must be opened or dissolved, this should be done by a professional trained in safe handling of hazardous drugs using appropriate equipment and safety procedures. Therefore a caregiver should not open or crush TEMODAR capsules at home without a provider-directed professional plan.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Teach safe home handling of temozolomide by keeping TEMODAR capsules intact and referring any needed opening or dissolution to trained hazardous-drug professionals.
semantic_correction.source_organization: DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine / FDA-approved labeling
semantic_correction.source_document_title: TEMODAR (temozolomide) capsules and TEMODAR for injection — Full Prescribing Information
semantic_correction.source_locator: Section 5.6 Exposure to Opened Capsules — do not open, chew, or dissolve; swallow whole with water; avoid powder contact with skin or mucous membranes; if capsules must be opened/dissolved, procedure should be performed by a professional trained in safe hazardous-drug handling using appropriate equipment and safety procedures. Section 17 Patient Counseling Information reinforces avoiding inhalation and skin/mucous-membrane contact
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: TEMODAR capsules should not be opened, chewed, or dissolved at home; if opening or dissolution is necessary, it should be performed by a trained hazardous-drug professional with appropriate equipment and safety procedures.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed the 'only' distractor cue, shortened the uniquely long correct answer, and anchored home handling to the February 2026 FDA-approved TEMODAR label.

audit_findings_append.source_locator: Section 5.6 Exposure to Opened Capsules; Section 17 Patient Counseling Information
audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — hazardous medication safety
audit_findings_append.finding: The original correct answer was uniquely longest and one distractor used absolute wording. The revised item directly tests label-mandated intact-capsule handling and professional hazardous-drug handling if opening is required.

option_audit.A: Correct. It matches the FDA-approved label's intact-capsule instruction and professional-handling requirement.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Ordinary examination gloves do not make caregiver opening of TEMODAR capsules an approved home practice.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Crushing or opening the capsule contradicts the label and increases powder exposure risk.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. The label specifically warns against inhalation and contact with skin or mucous membranes.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone follows the current TEMODAR label and directs swallowing difficulty back to the healthcare team rather than improvising hazardous-drug manipulation at home.
cueing_check: All four choices are caregiver handling plans of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.

checks: trained-professional requirement for necessary opening/dissolution verified directly
no caregiver PPE workaround treated as equivalent
